title: Garnet
subtitle: A Redis-compatible store evaluated for the memory service's hot path.

stats.label: lines of Rust run the managed instance from start to stop

lede: The memory service in FAFOHive keeps PostgreSQL as its source of truth and a Redis-protocol tier in front of it. Protocol compatibility is the seam. The service talks the Redis protocol. On my own host the tier is Redis. Garnet, Microsoft's Redis-compatible server, is wired in as an optional managed instance for that tier. It came in with a self-contained distribution build of the service, and it is a dedicated instance, never shared with any existing cache on the machine. This is a lifecycle adapter, not Garnet-specific engineering.
quote: The backing server is a deployment choice, not a code change.
evidence: Redis-protocol caching tiers: a hot tier for vector search, cached results and an observation write queue in front of PostgreSQL, with the backing server a deployment choice.
Rust systems engineering: a 242-line lifecycle module that starts a managed Garnet instance on localhost with its own port and checkpoints, waits for PING and stops with the service.
author: Corey James
